name: link-commands
title: Link Commands
description: Quicklinks as real files. Turn any link, folder or search into a Script Command you can version, grep and sync — then browse them grouped by environment, brand and category.
author: kud

commands.name: search-link-commands
commands.title: Search Link Commands
commands.subtitle: Link Commands
commands.description: Browse the link commands in your script directories, grouped by environment, brand and category, and run them.

commands.name: create-link-command
commands.title: Create Link Command
commands.subtitle: Link Commands
commands.description: Turn a link, a folder or a search URL into a Script Command, with its icon, brand, category and argument header filled in.

preferences.name: scriptDirectories
preferences.title: Script Directories
preferences.description: The folders holding your Script Commands, separated by a comma, a semicolon or a line break. These are the same folders you added under Raycast Settings > Extensions > Script Commands > Add Directories. You have to enter them again here because that list is stored in Raycast's encrypted database, and no public API exposes it — an extension simply cannot read it.

preferences.name: showBodyPreview
preferences.title: Detail Pane
preferences.label: Show the script source as well as the target
preferences.description: A link command's facts already sit in the table beside it, so its source is hidden by default — the body is a single open call and its header repeats the metadata. Turn this on to show it anyway. Commands that are not links always show their source.

preferences.name: groupCommands
preferences.title: Grouping
preferences.label: Group commands by environment, brand and category
preferences.description: Read the naming convention out of each command's title and subtitle — an @environment prefix on the title, a brand and a #category on the subtitle — and use it to build sections and filters. Commands that follow no convention are still listed; they simply have no environment or category.

preferences.name: terminalApplication
preferences.title: Terminal
preferences.description: The application used by the Run in Terminal action, which runs a script with its output left on screen — useful when a command misbehaves and you need to see its errors.

preferences.name: defaultAuthor
preferences.title: Author
preferences.description: Written into the @raycast.author header of Script Commands you create. Leave empty to omit it.

preferences.name: defaultAuthorURL
preferences.title: Author URL
preferences.description: Written into the @raycast.authorURL header of Script Commands you create. Leave empty to omit it.

scripts.prepublishOnly:
echo "

It seems like you are trying to publish the Raycast extension to npm.

If you did intend to publish it to npm, remove the \`prepublishOnly\` script and rerun \`npm publish\` again.
If you wanted to publish it to the Raycast Store instead, use \`npm run publish\` instead.

" && exit 1
